Unadjusted post-selection inference (UPSI)

infer_upsi.Rd

UPSI is sometimes referred to as "hybrid-OLS", but essentially we re-fit the selected model to the data as though we never used that same data to fit the model. It is common, easy, and ill-advised.

Usage

infer_upsi(
  object,
  data,
  nonselection = c("ignored", "confident_nulls", "uncertain_nulls"),
  conf.level = 0.95
)

Arguments

object

a selector object

data

the data used to fit the selector

nonselection

how to handle variables the selector did not select:

  • "ignored" (default): no inference; their estimate, ci_low, ci_high and p_value are NA.

  • "confident_nulls": treated as exactly zero, with estimate = 0, a degenerate interval [0, 0] and p_value = 1.

  • "uncertain_nulls": each non-selected variable is added, one at a time, to the selected model, which is refit on data; its estimate, interval and p-value come from that fit. These are not adjusted for selection.

Partial names are matched (e.g. "uncertain").

conf.level

.95 by default

Value

an inferrer object; see tidy.inferrer()
